text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use runs above peer rates at every complexity level above zero conditions, with a large share on low-complexity patients, but only three documented 99215 charts exist, so the pattern is suggestive and unconfirmed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward upcoding. The provider bills 99215 at roughly 1.5 to 2 times the all-provider share in every complexity band from one condition up, while matching peers only for patients with zero conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include routine diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection (C0069982, C0070240, C0071429), follow-up exams (C0070027, C0070347, C0071495) and low back pain (C0070319, C0071001), which do not obviously support high-complexity decision-making. Against this, the high-complexity sample (e.g., C0069995, C0070446) shows genuinely sick patients where 99215 is plausible. The records review cannot settle the question: only 3 documented 99215 claims came back, all supported at high MDM (C0070816, C0071119, C0071749), which is too thin to judge, and the few no-lab notes claiming moderate-plus data review are only weak signals. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above and check whether documented MDM or time actually supports level 5."}
